newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Akai mulls privatising Kong Wah.
newsitem.headline: Akai mulls privatising Kong Wah.

text.p: Akai Electric Co Ltd will raise its stake in Kong Wah Holdings Ltd to 96.7 percent from 77.3 percent and is considering privatising Kong Wah, the companies said in a joint statement on Tuesday.
"If Akai decides to effect a privatilisation of Kong Wah, an application will be made to the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Ltd for the delisting of the shares of Kong Wah," it said.
Kong Wah shares have been suspended from trade since October 5, 1995, as there was less than 25 percent of Kong Wah shares in public hands following a general offer by Akai.

Akai said it was considering the possibility of privatising Kong Wah after it agreed to buy 401.48 million Kong Wah shares, or 19.4 percent of Kong Wah's share capital, from companies controlled by Kong Wah's chairman and vice chairman.
Akai will pay HK$465.72 million for the shares, representing HK$1.16 per Kong Wah share, and will fund the purchase through internal resources.
Akai is 65.9 percent controlled by Semi-Tech (Global) Co Ltd.
The companies said a further announcement would be made concerning the privatisation proposal.
